plan.title: AD lesional vs control GO-BP over-representation
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is narrow: which GO biological processes are over-represented among the genes called significant in the delivered treated (AD lesional skin) versus control DESeq2 contrast. The primary input is therefore the delivered results table (/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, 12,000 genes x 8 columns, with base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change_se and p-values). No new differential test is fitted — the delivered contrast is taken as given, and its reference level and log2FC sign convention are stated explicitly before any direction-dependent claim is made.

Because the raw counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene-level Salmon output of unstated length-correction state) and the metadata (12 x 2, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) are also delivered, a sample-structure QC step runs first (T1S1): blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, per-sample library sizes and detected-gene counts. This exists to qualify the delivered result, not to re-derive it — specifically to see whether sample_01, whose library size is about 4x below the median, sits apart from its group. Per the low-depth rule the sample is kept and reported, not silently dropped; if it is an outlier that is a caveat on the enrichment, not a reason to refit.

T2S1 is the answer step: gene symbols from the results table mapped to Entrez with org.Hs.eg.db (unmapped share reported), the universe set to the genes actually tested in the delivered table rather than the genome, significance defined by the table's adjusted p-value at 0.05, and clusterProfiler::enrichGO run on the BP ontology with a 15-500 gene size window. Up- and down-regulated genes are tested as two separate lists, because pooling them mixes opposing biology in inflamed skin (barrier/lipid-metabolism genes down, immune/keratinization genes up in atopic dermatitis) and a pooled term cannot be interpreted directionally; a pooled run is reported alongside as a secondary view. The nested GO hierarchy returns many overlapping terms for one finding, so significant terms are reduced to representatives with rrvgo semantic similarity and the full table kept as a supplement. Two guardrails are built in: if fewer than ~50 genes pass significance in a direction, the over-representation test on that list has no power and the step must say so rather than report a term list; and the length/expression bias of a count-derived significant list is stated, with goseq available as a length-corrected sensitivity check if effective lengths are recoverable.

T1S3 assembles the report: the contrast and sign convention, the significant-list sizes, the universe, the size window, the collection and annotation releases, the redundancy collapse, the method-dependence caveat, and a full reproducibility record. The user asked only about GO BP, so no Hallmark/Reactome/WikiPathways pass and no ranked GSEA are planned as primary work — the enrichment step names GSEA on the full ranked list only as an explicitly secondary check when the significant list is too short to test.

steps.method: Blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
GO over-representation with clusterProfiler enrichGO and rrvgo term reduction
